safety_lead_time.comparison_action: REDUCE safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.57 days; current buffer exceeds statistical requirement

narrative:
Material PL1__MD4FDBA6 exhibits smooth demand behavior with moderate variability (CV=0.34), averaging 737 units per working day across 137 observations. The demand pattern shows no significant trend (p=0.5938) and follows a gamma distribution, making it well-suited for continuous review inventory policies.

Lead time stability is classified as unstable (CV=0.60), with mean delivery time of 1.58 days but high variance (σ=0.95 days). This volatility drives the need for substantial safety stock buffers to maintain the target 95% service level.

The EOQ model recommends an order quantity of 6,766 units, but storage capacity constraints (5540 units) force a reduction to 4,274 units. At 99.99% capacity utilization, this material is at the physical limit of available storage space, creating operational rigidity. Despite this constraint, the optimized policy delivers substantial cost savings of $25,345.87 annually (87.4% reduction) compared to the current SAP baseline that orders minimum quantities (331 units) with zero safety stock.

The recommended reorder point of 3,134 units and 6-day review cycle balance service level protection against the unstable lead time environment while respecting physical constraints. Lead time uncertainty is the dominant risk factor, with supplier variability contributing 40% of total variance.

research_insights.selected_model: Classical EOQ with lead time demand uncertainty
research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand regime (CV=0.34, 100% non-zero) with unstable lead time justifies continuous review (Q,r) policy. Gamma distribution approximation appropriate for moderate variability. Capacity constraint requires post-EOQ adjustment.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Material operates at 99.99% storage capacity, leaving no buffer for forecast errors or supply disruptions. Lead time CV of 0.60 places it near the threshold between moderate and unstable classification.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Capacity constraint binding - consider strategic discussion on storage expansion or alternative fulfillment models (VMI, consignment).
